notes.note: Read complete matching Tosatti2608.30153v2 text/image. Th1.1 is Vol(α−β)≥∫α^n−n∫α^(n−1)β for two nef real(1,1) classes on compact Kähler X, no projectivity assumption. Cor1.2 explicitly states orthogonality, locally C1,1 volume on the big cone with derivative n〈α^(n−1)〉·β, and pseudoeffective/movable cone duality. Movable cone is closed and generated by modification pushforwards of mixed Kähler products. The implications are attributed to BDPP/BFJ and Boucksom’s appendix to WN, not proved here yet. No non-Archimedean transfer or BJ22 repair follows.

Read complete matching Tosatti v2 text/image. C1,1 regularity is attributed to Cao–Tosatti with the newly supplied Morse inequality, only inside the big cone; boundary volume is merely locally Lipschitz. Cor1.3 relates numerical restricted divisor volume to movable pairing for big α. Cor1.4 identifies M with closure of the balanced cone and with the closed cone of single Kähler-power modification pushforwards; closure is essential. Proof strategy substitutes Lebesgue-null supported currents for unavailable pluripolar-supported currents, then couples mass concentration with a modified Lamari/Hahn–Banach lemma. Lebesgue-null support need not be pluripolar. AI discussion acknowledgment is not an independent verification.

Read complete matching Tosatti v2 text/image. Prop2.1 uses finitely many locally cancelling potentials Φi=max(ci−φi,0) and Φ=maxΦi, with all positive regions covering X. Generic constants avoid countably many constant transition differences; nonconstant pluriharmonic differences have null real-analytic level sets. Unique-max regions have ω+i∂bar∂Φ=0, so the positive closed current is supported on the closed null tie set. Lebesgue-null rather than pluripolar support is explicit. Compactness is used for finite maxima and a stable covering choice. Ambient dimension n=1 is separated before the higher-dimensional proof. Lebesgue decomposition is positive and coefficientwise linear, but its pieces need not be closed.

Difference C−F is shown closed by local mass bounds and compact K minus closed F, not the false general claim that a sum of two closed sets is closed.
